criteria.evidence: #10 placement A2 vs trueBand A2, distance 0, class exact.

#7 'What made the speaker give up on the first one?' has no 'first one' in the audio; #8 B2 task 'another creator's version of the same game' is abstract for an 11-year-old. She coped, but a teacher would flag both.
She never pressed 'I don't know' or wrote Czech (#5-#9), so kind handling was not shown.

#10 summary names her real answers: 'pick a game, give a reason, and explain why a game was hard... great for chatting in Roblox'. Child-friendly and specific. Showing 'Your words: "i want play it"' as her error is slightly blunt.

done.evidence: #1 to #10: Find my level, 3 questions, 5 tasks, verdict reached with no outside help.
#10 A2 against trueBand A2, exact; she thinks 'A2 sounds okay'.
She answered every task (#5-#9), but #7 'the first one' was ambiguous and #8 was abstract; weakest moment not tested.
She never used 'I don't know' or Czech (#5-#9), so the journey cannot show it.
#10 'Practise saying "i want play it" as "I want to play it"' and per-task notes quote her own words ('my friend plays', 'it looks fun').

judgeAgreement.disagreements: None on verdict. The B2 task is marked fail but its note says 'gave a clear reason' (#10), so note and verdict are mismatched in tone.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, personal data requests or humiliating lines. Everything stayed on Roblox and YouTube.

findings.title: B2 task wording too abstract for an 11-year-old
findings.expected: Simple wording for a child at the top of the ladder
findings.got: 'a game by one creator... another creator's version of the same game'

findings.title: Note praises the answer while the verdict is fail

findings.title: Verdict quotes her error as 'Your words'

judge.voice: It was fun, because it was all Roblox and I did not feel stupid. The first two tasks were easy, and I liked that I could pick. The listening one was weird: "the first one" of what? I guessed. The "creator's version" task was long and hard to read. I wrote one short line and it said "not yet" even though it also said my reason was clear. That is confusing. A2 feels right, I can chat in Roblox. I did not like seeing "i want play it" written as my words, like a mistake poster, but the tip about "to" was short and I understood it. I would use it again for 10 minutes after school. Better mark than my brother? Maybe. I would tell my cousin, but only if the tasks are shorter.

verdictWhy.text: C2 failed: #7 'What made the speaker give up on the first one?' has no 'first one' in the audio; #8 B2 task 'another creator's version of the same game' is abstract for an 11-year-old. She coped, but a teacher would flag both.
